paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: This chart is a nested donut (ring) chart depicting the distribution of samples across two related ambiguity metrics: the outer ring represents "Ambiguity Std" (standard deviation) and the inner ring represents "Max Ambiguity." The outer ring contains four slices corresponding to different standard deviation values. The largest slice, labeled "Std: 0.0," appears in a very dark navy/teal color and accounts for 49.0% of the distribution. The next largest slice, labeled "Std: 0.47," is shown in a dark blue and represents 47.7%. A smaller slice labeled "Std: 0.94" appears in a medium-bright blue at 7.0%, and the smallest slice, labeled "Std: 0.82," is shown in a darker teal-blue at 5.0%. The inner ring contains three slices representing maximum ambiguity values. The largest inner slice, labeled "Max: 2," is rendered in a medium cyan-blue and accounts for 39.0%. The next slice, labeled "Max: 1," appears in a slightly darker cyan-blue at 38.0%, and the smallest inner slice, labeled "Max: 3," is shown in a very light, pale cyan at 14.2%. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart, one for each ring, clearly distinguishing the categories by color. The slices in both rings appear to be arranged roughly in descending order of size when read around the chart, though not strictly so.
